editorial:
Imagine being a good cop in a city where your own boss is actually the bad guy. That is exactly the mess you get into here. You follow a small group of honest officers in the anti-drug unit who realize their superiors are stealing money and working with criminals. It starts as a police procedural but quickly turns into a wild ride when the corrupt bosses frame the good guys for murder. Now, you are on the run from both the gangs and your own teammates, making the whole vibe feel tense and desperate from the start.

What really makes this pop is the action. Since Yuen Woo-ping is directing, the fights are top-notch and feel punchy. The pacing is quick, though some of the plot twists can feel a bit convenient. If you love old-school Hong Kong cinema with gritty streets and loud explosions, you will love this. For the best experience, try to find the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection so you can see all the detail in the fight scenes, or look for it to rent on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head in a huge final showdown where the honest cops finally trap the corrupt leaders. After a series of intense fights and gun battles, the bad bosses are exposed in front of everyone. The heroes manage to clear their names and prove they were framed all along. Most of the villains end up dead or behind bars, and the good cops finally get to breathe easy knowing the department is clean.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s action movies and martial arts fights.
